forces.title: European demographic shifts weaken packaging consumption growth
forces.description: Projected population decline in the EU, alongside an increasing share of residents aged 65 and older, is expected to reduce consumption growth across several end markets for packaging. This demographic shift reshapes demand mix, potentially favoring specific packaging types over others, impacting overall volumes for flexible and rigid packaging manufacturers.
forces.source_title: Reinventing the European pulp and paper operating model

forces.title: Complex regulatory environment impacts packaging production in Europe
forces.description: The European packaging industry faces an increasingly complex regulatory environment, driven by sustainability demands. New regulations on materials, waste management, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), and mandates for reusable/recyclable packaging (e.g., EU PPWR by 2030) are shifting sustainability from a differentiator to a baseline requirement. This necessitates significant investment and adaptation for flexible and rigid packaging producers.
forces.source_title: Reinventing the European pulp and paper operating model

forces.title: Volatile input and energy costs strain packaging margins
forces.description: The packaging sector, including flexible and rigid producers, continues to face elevated and volatile input costs for raw materials (fibers, chemicals) and energy. Geopolitical developments and supply disruptions have amplified cost pressures, with energy competitiveness being a major differentiator. This volatility compresses margins and requires advanced operational and procurement strategies to mitigate the impact on production costs.
forces.source_title: Reinventing the European pulp and paper operating model

forces.title: Growing global competition limits European packaging price recovery
forces.description: Europe’s packaging industry faces intensified global competition, particularly from Asia, which acts as a structural export platform. Excess supply from capacity additions in Asia flowing into international markets limits opportunities for European producers to achieve sustained price recovery across various packaging grades, including those in flexible and rigid segments, thereby exerting downward pressure on market prices.
forces.source_title: Reinventing the European pulp and paper operating model

forces.title: Key barriers impede sustainable packaging adoption across value chain
forces.description: Packaging purchasers and consumers face persistent barriers hindering the widespread adoption of sustainable packaging solutions for both flexible and rigid formats. These include concerns over affordability, potential performance trade-offs, lack of alignment on sustainability definitions, regulatory uncertainty, limited or unreliable supply of sustainable materials, and insufficient knowledge of available solutions, delaying market transition.
forces.source_title: No ordinary disruption: State of the packaging and paper industry

forces.title: Evolving tariffs projected to slow global packaging growth
forces.description: Forecasts from 2025 estimate that evolving tariffs could reduce global packaging growth by up to 0.5 percent per annum. This factor particularly affects packaging segments, including flexible and rigid, that are heavily dependent on imports. Combined with regionalization efforts, tariffs are reshaping trade flows and increasing cost pressures for European producers.
forces.source_title: No ordinary disruption: State of the packaging and paper industry

forces.title: Consumers prioritize price/quality over sustainability in purchasing decisions
forces.description: Global consumer surveys from 2020-2025 consistently show that sustainability factors have declined in importance, now ranking among the bottom three considerations. Price and quality are the most critical product characteristics influencing purchasing decisions. This shift, driven by macroeconomic uncertainties and inflationary pressures, constrains consumers' willingness to pay more for sustainable flexible and rigid packaging.
forces.source_title: No ordinary disruption: State of the packaging and paper industry

forces.title: CPGs exert pricing pressure and shift inventory risk to packaging suppliers
forces.description: Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) companies are reconfiguring operating models due to slower demand and cost pressures. This translates into suppliers, including flexible and rigid packaging manufacturers, facing demands for shorter pricing resets and more index-based mechanisms. CPGs are also reducing working capital, increasing order volatility, and shifting inventory risk upstream to packaging producers.
forces.source_title: No ordinary disruption: State of the packaging and paper industry

forces.title: Oversupply creates persistent pricing pressure for plastic packaging
forces.description: Both rigid and flexible plastic packaging segments face significant oversupply conditions. For rigid plastics, this combines with soft CPG demand to deteriorate profitability. In flexible packaging, despite innovation, oversupply puts pressure on pricing. This market imbalance requires plastic packaging manufacturers to focus intensely on cost efficiency, commercial excellence, and product differentiation to maintain margins.
forces.source_title: No ordinary disruption: State of the packaging and paper industry

forces.title: Metal packaging gains market share through intrinsic advantages
forces.description: The metal packaging segment, encompassing aluminium and steel cans within rigid packaging, continues to achieve steady volume growth and capture market share. This trend is driven by strong consumer and industry preferences for metal's key attributes, including portability, high recyclability, and its ability to convey premiumization for various products, making it a competitive choice over other substrates.
forces.source_title: No ordinary disruption: State of the packaging and paper industry

forces.title: High interest rates constrain investments and increase refinancing risk
forces.description: Materially higher interest rates have significantly increased interest expenses for packaging companies, impacting those with high leverage acquired at peak valuations (2019-2021). With flat or declining operating performance, interest coverage has sharply deteriorated, elevating refinancing risk as debt maturities approach. This constrains companies' ability to make growth investments and necessitates liquidity preservation and covenant management.
forces.source_title: No ordinary disruption: State of the packaging and paper industry

forces.title: Industry consolidation accelerates with focus on roll-up strategies
forces.description: The packaging industry is undergoing strong consolidation, with an increase in fewer but larger and more strategic transactions, often financed by equity. many companies are adopting 'roll-up' strategies, acquiring smaller packaging firms to build consolidated, scalable platforms focused on one or two key product lines, departing from previous diversification across many subsectors in flexible and rigid packaging.
forces.source_title: Reigniting growth through M&A: A playbook for paper and packaging companies

forces.title: Rapid Gen AI adoption set to boost packaging growth
forces.description: The packaging industry is swiftly adopting Generative AI (Gen AI), moving from experimentation to active implementation. Over 80% of leaders reported ongoing Gen AI initiatives in 2025. This rapid embrace is expected to fuel growth, particularly in commercial excellence (sales, marketing, customer service), procurement, and supply chain/logistics, promising significant revenue uplift and operational efficiencies for flexible and rigid packaging companies.
forces.source_title: Rewiring the packaging industry: Gen AI and commercial excellence

forces.title: Food & Drink sector automation boosts packaging line demand
forces.description: The Food & Drink sector in Ireland is accelerating automation, including packaging lines and robotics, to counter rising cost pressures and staff shortages. This trend leads to existing staff being upskilled and production previously outsourced being brought in-house. This drives demand for advanced and efficient packaging machinery and solutions for flexible and rigid packaging manufacturers.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Food and Drink Sector H2 2025 Insights and H1 2026 Outlook

forces.title: Distilleries diversify with new packaging formats like pouches
forces.description: The global spirits market, facing high competitiveness, sees distilleries diversifying their ranges with innovative blending, Ready to Drink (RTD) offerings, and adopting new packaging formats such as pouches. This specific adoption of flexible packaging solutions by a significant end-user industry represents a direct growth opportunity and upside driver for manufacturers of pouches and similar flexible containers, as noted in an Irish context.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Food and Drink Sector H2 2025 Insights and H1 2026 Outlook

forces.title: Softening global base metal prices reduce input costs for metal packaging
forces.description: The metals sector in Ireland anticipates softening global base metal prices. While a headwind for metal producers, this trend acts as a tailwind for flexible and rigid packaging manufacturers, specifically those producing aluminium and steel cans. Reduced raw material costs offer an opportunity for improved margins or competitive pricing in metal packaging as input costs decrease.

viewpoints.title: European packaging grades show resilience with selective value-driven growth
viewpoints.description: McKinsey's Packaging & Paper Practice notes that while graphic paper contracts, packaging and specialty grades in Europe remain more resilient. However, growth is becoming more selective within packaging. The anticipated shift from plastics to fiber-based solutions is occurring more slowly than expected. Value, rather than volume, is now the primary growth driver, implying a focus on higher-value flexible and rigid packaging solutions.
viewpoints.source_title: Reinventing the European pulp and paper operating model

viewpoints.title: Overall packaging industry faces widespread deceleration in growth and margins
viewpoints.description: McKinsey reports that the global packaging and paper industry, encompassing plastics, metal, and glass, entered a reset after 2022. It faces flat to declining volumes, external shocks like tariffs, volatile raw material prices, and cautious consumer spending. This has led to decelerated growth and near-flat or slightly negative EBITDA margins across all major substrates, indicating widespread underperformance in the packaging sector.
viewpoints.source_title: No ordinary disruption: State of the packaging and paper industry

viewpoints.title: Rigid plastics profitability deteriorating due to soft demand and overcapacity
viewpoints.description: The rigid plastics segment of the packaging industry is experiencing significant pressure. Soft demand from Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) companies, coupled with persistent overcapacity, has led to sustained pricing pressure. This environment has resulted in a deterioration of profitability across many segments of rigid plastic packaging, particularly within blow molding, necessitating a focus on cost and differentiation to remain competitive.
viewpoints.source_title: No ordinary disruption: State of the packaging and paper industry

viewpoints.title: Flexible packaging innovation countered by intense pricing pressure from oversupply
viewpoints.description: Flexible packaging benefits from continuous innovation, such as the development of mono-materials and recycle-ready structures, which helps maintain customer engagement and strengthens sustainability positioning. However, similar to rigid plastics, the segment is burdened by oversupply. This market imbalance is exerting considerable pressure on pricing, requiring companies to enhance commercial excellence, cost management, and differentiated capabilities to sustain profitability.
viewpoints.source_title: No ordinary disruption: State of the packaging and paper industry

viewpoints.title: Metal packaging sustains volume growth, gaining share through key attributes
viewpoints.description: The metal packaging segment continues to exhibit steady volume growth, with certain categories gaining market share. This positive trend is attributed to metal's inherent advantages in portability, high recyclability, and its appeal for premiumization trends. These attributes position metal packaging (e.g., aluminium and steel cans) favorably in the current market, contributing to its sustained performance compared to other packaging substrates.
viewpoints.source_title: No ordinary disruption: State of the packaging and paper industry

viewpoints.title: Glass packaging faces weak demand, with growth limited to premium segments
viewpoints.description: Glass packaging is experiencing relatively weak overall demand, primarily driven by ongoing substitution towards alternative packaging substrates and reduced consumption in large end-use segments like spirits and wine. Despite these challenges, attractive growth pockets persist within the premium packaging market, such as for perfumes and high-end fermented beverages, offering specific opportunities amidst a declining broader market for glass containers.
viewpoints.source_title: No ordinary disruption: State of the packaging and paper industry

viewpoints.title: Packaging industry rapidly adopting Generative AI for operational and commercial gains
viewpoints.description: The packaging industry is quickly moving from experimenting with Generative AI (Gen AI) to actively implementing solutions. A 2025 survey revealed over 80% of leaders have Gen AI initiatives under consideration, in development, or launched. This rapid deployment indicates strong belief in Gen AI's potential to drive growth, with anticipated revenue gains of 8% or more in commercial excellence alone for packaging companies, including those in flexible and rigid segments.
viewpoints.source_title: Rewiring the packaging industry: Gen AI and commercial excellence

demand_drivers.description: Packaging underpins modern commerce and daily life, enabling the safe, efficient movement of goods across industrial and consumer supply chains globally.

new_opportunities.description: Anticipated revenue gains of 8% or more from Gen AI implementation, driven by identifying and prioritizing leads, and generating market reports to optimize sales and customer engagement for flexible and rigid packaging products.

Anticipated revenue gains of 3-5% from Gen AI implementation, driven by generating customized market trend reports and building detailed RFx packages from technical specifications, enhancing cost efficiency for packaging material sourcing.

Anticipated revenue gains of 6-8% from Gen AI implementation, with high-impact opportunities in inventory health assessment and shipment status chatbots, improving efficiency and reducing waste in packaging supply chains.

market_sizing.methodology: Survey of packaging leaders in US and Europe regarding anticipated revenue gains from Gen AI implementation across commercial excellence, procurement, and supply chain/logistics functions. The data applies to the packaging industry generally, including IN020702.

demand_drivers.description: Macroeconomic uncertainty and cautious consumer spending lead to reduced purchasing, directly impacting demand for packaged goods and thus packaging.
Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) companies are restructuring operations due to slower demand and cost pressures, influencing their packaging requirements and volumes.

pnl_drivers.description: Consumers prioritizing value for money reduces willingness to pay for premium or sustainable packaging, impacting margins for flexible and rigid packaging suppliers.
CPG companies demand shorter pricing resets and index-based mechanisms, putting continuous pressure on packaging manufacturers' profitability.
CPG companies are taking working capital out of supply chains, increasing order volatility and shifting inventory risk upstream to packaging producers, impacting operational efficiency and costs.
